question: Which Linux companion app direction should OpenClaw accept as the canonical path now that Windows Hub ships externally?
rationale: Current main solves the Windows desktop-app side through Windows Hub, but Linux still needs an architecture, packaging, ownership, and security stance before an implementation PR can be scoped safely.

options.title: GTK/libadwaita Linux app
options.body: Proceed with a native Linux companion app aligned with the issue discussion and require distro-packaged dependency, gateway pairing, tray, and security proof before landing.

options.title: Shared desktop shell
options.body: Revive a shared Tauri-style Linux/Windows desktop shell only if maintainers accept the extra WebView/Rust dependency and release-surface cost.

options.title: Split Linux capability issues
options.body: Close the umbrella only after creating narrower Linux app capability trackers for notifications, tray/status, node mode, packaging, and onboarding.

recommendation.title: GTK/libadwaita Linux app
recommendation.body: Proceed with a native Linux companion app aligned with the issue discussion and require distro-packaged dependency, gateway pairing, tray, and security proof before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete opened the issue, gave the clearest Linux product-direction comments, and owns recent platform status docs.
